name: Cataract-microcornea syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of microcornea defined as corneal diameter less than 10 mm
Bilateral congenital cataracts present at birth or early infancy
No evidence of other ocular malformations such as microphthalmia or anterior segment dysgenesis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of both microcornea and congenital cataract without other major ocular anomalies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and based on ophthalmological examination; genetic testing may assist in differential diagnosis

imaging: Slit-lamp examination showing microcornea and cataract
Ultrasound biomicroscopy to assess anterior segment structures
other: Visual evoked potentials may show decreased response due to cataract-induced visual impairment

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of microphthalmia with reduced globe size
More extensive ocular malformations than isolated microcornea
Anterior segment abnormalities including iris and angle malformations
Often associated with glaucoma and other systemic anomalies

redFlags: Presence of systemic abnormalities suggesting syndromic association
references: Shiels A, Hejtmancik JF. Genetics of congenital cataract. Eur J Hum Genet. 2017;25(10):1141-1147.
Francis PJ, Berry V, Bhattacharya SS. Congenital cataracts: molecular genetics, clinical features, disease mechanisms and novel therapeutic approaches. Br J Ophthalmol. 2000;84(7):737-742.
